title: only quarter americans think iran war is worthwhile reutersipsos poll shows 2026 09 04
text:
What happened this week
Fears of renewed escalation in the war between the United States and Iran have grown after a weekend exchange of fire — the first since July — and a barrage of U.S. airstrikes on Tuesday prompted Iranian retaliation.
An explosion that ripped through a wedding celebration in southern Iran on Monday, which killed four people and injured at least 68 others, likely resulted from a direct hit by a U.S. munition, a Reuters visual investigation shows.
What the numbers show
Only a quarter of Americans think the war in Iran has been worthwhile — similar to views about the wars in Afghanistan and Iraq that began in the early 2000s, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll that ended Monday.
What's next
With U.S. midterm elections looming, top aides to President Donald Trump are pushing to keep the unpopular conflict from escalating and dominating the news, sources told Reuters. Republicans are campaigning to defend thin majorities in both houses of Congress.
Trump said on Wednesday that the renewed ​U.S. campaign against Iran ‌would not continue for "too long." He also reiterated his position that the upcoming elections were not factoring into his Iran strategy.
